    StartersRoast pork and provolone slidersGarlic fennel roast pork, broccolini and provolone on small bunsHow to make it1kg pork shoulder1 garlic bulb2 sprigs of rosemary1 tsp fennel seeds2 bunches of broccolini1 red chilli, sliced150g sharp provolone, sliced12 slider buns2 tbsp olive oilRub the pork with garlic, rosemary and fennel seeds.Roast at 160°C for 3 hours. Rest and slice thin.Fry the broccolini in the olive oil with garlic and chilli.Pile the pork, greens and provolone into the buns and spoon over the pan juices.Birthday party pigs in blanketsThe birthday party that goes wrong for ColeHow to make itAs written, serves 4Cocktail frankfurts rolled in buttery puff pastry with a sesame top, baked golden and served hot with honey mustard and tomato relish for dipping.Heat the oven to 200°C.Cut 2 sheets of puff pastry into 24 strips.Wrap each strip around a cocktail frankfurt and sit seam side down on a lined tray.Brush with beaten egg and scatter with sesame seeds.Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until puffed and golden.Mix 3 tbsp Dijon mustard with 2 tbsp honey and serve alongside a bowl of tomato relish.Pierogies with sour cream and onionLynn turns around and every cupboard is open.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsAnniversary salmon with beurre blancRoast salmon in beurre blanc with crushed baby potatoesHow to make it4 salmon fillets800g baby potatoes2 tbsp olive oil1 shallot, finely diced100ml white wine2 tbsp white wine vinegar150g cold butter, diced2 bunches of asparagusHeat the oven to 220°C. Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes, drain and crush with olive oil and salt.Season the salmon and roast skin side down on an oiled tray for 8 minutes.Simmer the shallot in the wine and vinegar until a couple of tablespoons are left. Whisk in the cold butter a piece at a time over low heat.Blanch the asparagus for 2 minutes. Plate up and spoon the sauce over the fish.Lynn's kitchen buttermilk pancakesLynn turns her back for a second and every cupboard is openHow to make itAs written, serves 4Fluffy buttermilk pancakes stacked high with crisp streaky bacon, a pat of salted butter, fresh blueberries and plenty of warm maple syrup.Whisk 300g plain flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarb and a pinch of salt.Whisk in 500ml buttermilk, 2 eggs and 50g melted butter until just combined and rest for 10 minutes.Fry 12 rashers of streaky bacon until crisp and keep warm.Brush a clean pan with butter and cook 80ml ladles of batter over medium heat for 2 minutes until bubbles show, then flip for 1 minute.Stack with the bacon, butter, blueberries and warm maple syrup.SweetsGhostly white chocolate mousseWhite chocolate mousse set in glasses, topped with raspberriesHow to make it150g white chocolate300ml thickened cream1 egg white100g raspberriesMelt the chocolate into a third of the cream, warmed, and cool.Whip the rest of the cream and whisk the egg white. Fold both through the chocolate.Spoon into glasses and set in the fridge for 4 hours.Top with a few raspberries.Red tent chocolate strawberriesStrawberries dipped in dark chocolate and rolled in crushed freeze-dried raspberriesHow to make it500g dry strawberries150g dark chocolate1 packet freeze-dried raspberries, crushedMelt the chocolate.Dip each strawberry in the chocolate.Before it sets, roll half of each in the crushed raspberries so they are bright red.Chill on baking paper until set.DrinksPhilly winter hot spiced apple ciderApple juice simmered with cinnamon, cloves, star anise and orange, no alcoholHow to make it1.5 L cloudy apple juice6 cinnamon sticks6 whole cloves3 star anises2 oranges, sliced2 tbsp brown sugar120ml dark rum, optional for the adults' mugsPut the apple juice, two of the cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise, half the orange slices and the sugar in a pot.Bring to a simmer, then hold just below a simmer for 20 minutes.Strain into mugs and add a cinnamon stick and orange slice to each.
